models.name: Qwen3.8-27B (MLX-Serve 26.10.1, drafter on)
models.full_name: Qwen3.8-27B 4-bit on MLX-Serve 26.10.1 with its drafter (M4 Max)
models.why: Three Apple-Silicon engines on one Qwen3.8-27B 4-bit model and one drafter land within a few t/s of each other: TensorFold 154 t/s on numbers, mlx-serve 115 on code and 54 on a story workload, and all three fall to 29-31 t/s with drafting off, so the race is the drafter, not the engine.

engines.quant: Qwen3.8-27B 4-bit (ddalcu's build), drafting on, code workload, --no-mtp
engines.engine_min_version: mlx-serve 26.10.1 --no-mtp (default 26.10.1 picks MTP over the DFlash drafter)

models.name: Qwen3.8-27B (TensorFold + DFlash2, Mac mini M6)
models.full_name: Qwen3.8-27B 4-bit on TensorFold with DFlash2 drafting on a Mac mini M6
models.why: Speculative decoding stopped being a cloud trick: the same Qwen3.8-27B MLX 4-bit on a Mac mini M6 goes from 10.1 to 61.9 t/s on code generation and 10.1 to 30.8 on chat with TensorFold's DFlash2 drafting, with every accepted token byte-identical to serial decoding.

models.name: Qwen3.8-27B (Apple Silicon long-context)
models.full_name: Qwen3.8-27B on Apple Silicon with the drafter enabled
models.why: A runtime update alone made Qwen3.8-27B substantially faster on Apple Silicon — +66 percent on an M5 Ultra, +28 on an M4 Max, +37 on an M1 Pro with the drafter on — while MLX-Serve kept output byte-identical across 18 models.

engines.hardware: M5 Max MacBook Pro (LM Studio Bionic serving)
engines.quant: Inco AI Splash engine, subagent running alongside the main agent

models.name: Qwen3.8-27B (TensorFold M3 Ultra)
models.full_name: Qwen3.8-27B 4-bit on TensorFold + DFlash2 vs stock MLX on an M3 Ultra
models.why: Yves LaRose's benchmark shows TensorFold finished 256-token replies only 3.8-5.3 percent sooner than stock MLX at 8K-32K on an M3 Ultra — and the real gap was context reuse, where a 64GiB cache cut a repeated 64K-context request from 632s to 16s.

models.name: Qwen3.8-27B Coder390
models.why: A modified 27B coder tuned to cut unproductive reasoning tails (LiveCodeBench 83 to 90): DFlash2 speculative decoding pushes it to 180 t/s on a 24GB GPU.

engines.quant: DFlash2 speculative decoding, Coder390 EfficientThink-based tune
